requirement:
Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded
assessment read merely to account for their existence. A missing annotation or
recorded read produces no warning or validation error solely because the item
exists.

`habeas status` and `habeas author` do not report unreferenced-item counts or
warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history to decide whether source
items have been read.

This does not waive the reference-role obligations of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure`, the annotation requirements for tests
and Cargo examples under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples`, or execution-coverage policy
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Actual assessment reads
remain dependencies checked for freshness under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` states only observable behavior, so it has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. I checked each clause for one that prescribes how the code is built:

- Clause: "Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded assessment read merely to account for their existence." It also says a missing annotation or recorded read produces no warning or validation error solely because the item exists. These clauses describe what Habeas does and doesn't report. A tool could reach the same result through any internal design, so they prescribe no library, algorithm, type, signature or delegation.
- Clause: "`habeas status` and `habeas author` do not report unreferenced-item counts or warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history." This is also observable behavior. It names two commands but only says what their output omits. It does not prescribe how they are built. A command could drop or restructure its internals and still satisfy it.
- Clause: the closing paragraph says the requirement does not waive the obligations of `requirements.references.procedure`, `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `requirements.references.coverage.examples`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` and `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`. These are cited context. Each of them is judged against its own text. The note that actual reads stay freshness-checked dependencies refers to `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`, which owns that obligation.

The supplied review roots are empty. No structural obligation needs an implementation root here, so the absence of implementation edges is not a gap.

behavioral: Obligations and the tests that cover them:

1. Rust functions, methods, structs, enums and unions need no annotation, and a missing annotation produces no warning or validation error. `tests/coverage.rs#fn[ordinary_functions_types_and_test_helpers_require_no_book_connection]` writes a struct, enum, union, trait method, inherent method, free function and nested-module helper with no references. It asserts that `validate_repository` reports no error mentioning "coverage" or "no {test}". It also asserts that `status_markdown` has no coverage warnings, no "has no recent coverage" and no "nodes have coverage warnings", for both `all=false` and `all=true`. `tests/references.rs#fn[disallowed_paths_are_skipped_and_projects_outside_git_scan_every_file]` shows that an unreferenced `fn uncited` in scanned files produces no "function uncited" error. `tests/references.rs#fn[habeas_util_citations_cover_their_item_without_a_citation_review]` and `tests/references.rs#fn[fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated]` assert that items with no or with built-in references get no coverage error.

2. `habeas status` reports no unreferenced-item counts or warnings. `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_retains_repository_findings_without_indexing_unreferenced_functions]` adds an unreferenced `fn unread` and runs `status` with every flag combination (none, `--all`, `--verbose`, `--all --verbose`) and with and without a selection. It runs from a nested directory. It asserts there is no "has no recent coverage" and no "coverage warnings", and that other repository findings are still reported.

3. `habeas author` reports no unreferenced-item counts or warnings and does not inspect evidence Git history. `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[dumb_terminal_keeps_plain_batch_diagnostics]` adds an unreferenced `ordinary_helper` and commits it to Git. It authors, and asserts that stderr has no "coverage warnings" or "coverage history is incomplete" and that stdout is exactly the summary line. It then commits the evidence, so Git history exists. It runs `status --all` and `author --all`, and asserts the output has none of "coverage warnings", "coverage history", "unreferenced" or "ordinary_helper". It also asserts that no additional assessments are issued. This covers both the "no history inspection" and "no counts" clauses as far as they are observable.

4. Parse failures still being reported (`tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference]`, `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_all_files_and_parse_failures]`) and discovery behavior (`tests/references.rs#fn[working_directory_references_count_immediately_and_follow_nested_ignore_rules]`) are extra context and are marked correctly.

The "does not waive" paragraph cites other requirements (`requirements.references.procedure`, `requirements.references.coverage.tests`, `requirements.references.coverage.examples`, the test-coverage checks and `requirements.ci.outline_inputs`). These are context, so I did not reassess them. The example-target check is still exercised by `tests/coverage.rs#fn[untracked_examples_are_checked_as_cargo_targets]`, which confirms that the waiver does not remove the Cargo example obligation.

I found no obligation that lacks a test with a relevant assertion, and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} rust_item_coverage
Rust functions, methods, structs, enums, and unions need no annotation or recorded
assessment read merely to account for their existence. A missing annotation or
recorded read produces no warning or validation error solely because the item
exists.
`habeas status` and `habeas author` do not report unreferenced-item counts or
warnings, and do not inspect evidence-file Git history to decide whether source
items have been read.
This does not waive the reference-role obligations of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure`, the annotation requirements for tests
and Cargo examples under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.examples`, or execution-coverage policy
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Actual assessment reads
remain dependencies checked for freshness under
{cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`.
:::{req} procedure
A {term}`requirements.references.source_item` MUST choose its references under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`
for each candidate definition by this procedure, and MAY carry several:
1. For tests, apply {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and use
`{test}` for each definition the test is designed to verify. A helper reached
from a marked test needs no separate reference.
2. For source items demonstrating a requirement’s structural obligations, follow
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_markers`. An item that is a site of
a distributed definition under {cite}`requirements.references.distributed`
needs no reference to it solely for being a site.
3. Otherwise, if the item should be re-checked or kept in sync when the
definition changes, it MUST use `{cite}`.
Other source items need no reference. In particular, helpers reached from
implementation roots or tests need no individual annotation or assessment read
merely to account for their existence. Reviewers still inspect relevant helpers
when judging tests under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`.
A `{fixme}` reference is added independently of this procedure.
:::{req} coverage.tests
Every {term}`requirements.references.test_source_item` MUST carry one or more
`{test}` annotations in comments belonging to that item under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{req} coverage.examples
Every Cargo example target, each `.rs` file directly under the package's
`examples/` directory, each `examples/<name>/main.rs`, and each `[[example]]`
`path` in `Cargo.toml`, MUST `{cite}` a named example of the book under
{cite}`requirements.examples.definition` in a comment in that file. An example
target without one MUST be a validation error naming the file.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. For display and reference coverage, it MUST derive the inclusive line range
from the first and last bytes of the SDK outline item's attachment-inclusive
span under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span`. An empty
span covers the line at its start. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
:::{definition} test_source_item
:phrase: test source item
A {term}`requirements.references.source_item` recognized as a test by Habeas.
In first-party Rust sources under {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`,
this is a function with `#[test]` or an attribute whose path ends in `test`,
such as `#[tokio::test]`. This includes functions in Cargo integration-test targets.
